subUnits.title: 6.1 Expressions pour Donner son Opinion
notes: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to: express personal opinions using standard French phrases.
- JE CROIS QUE... (I believe that...) — followed by 'que' before the opinion
- JE PENSE QUE... (I think that...) — followed by 'que' before the opinion
- À MON AVIS... (in my opinion...) — stands ALONE, NO 'que' needed
- These phrases signal to the listener that a PERSONAL VIEWPOINT is about to follow, not a stated fact.
- Je crois que c'est une bonne idée. (I believe that it's a good idea.)
- À mon avis, c'est bon. (In my opinion, it's good.)
je crois QUE... | je pense QUE... → 'que' is REQUIRED
à mon avis... → NO 'que' — stands alone, directly followed by opinion

Opinion phrases are like different doorways into the SAME room (your personal viewpoint): 'je crois que' and 'je pense que' have a small step ('que') you must cross before entering, while 'à mon avis' is a doorway you can walk straight through with no extra step.
- Forgetting 'que' after 'je crois' or 'je pense' (e.g., 'je pense c'est bon' instead of 'je pense QUE c'est bon').
- Incorrectly adding 'que' after 'à mon avis,' which stands alone.

quiz.explanation: 'Je crois que' means I believe that — followed by 'que' before stating the opinion.
'Je pense que' means I think that — followed by 'que' before stating the opinion.
'À mon avis' means in my opinion — it stands alone with NO 'que' following.

quiz.q: Which word follows 'je crois' and 'je pense' before stating the opinion?
quiz.explanation: Both 'je crois' and 'je pense' must be followed by 'que' before the opinion itself.

quiz.q: Does 'à mon avis' need 'que' before the opinion?
quiz.explanation: 'À mon avis' stands ALONE — 'que' is never needed after it.

quiz.q: How would you say 'I believe that it is a good idea'?
opts: Je crois que c'est une bonne idée
Je crois à c'est une bonne idée
Je crois de c'est une bonne idée
Je crois c'est une bonne idée
quiz.explanation: 'Je crois QUE c'est une bonne idée' — 'que' is required between 'crois' and the opinion.

quiz.q: How would you say 'in my opinion, it's good'?
opts: À mon avis de c'est bon
À mon avis que c'est bon
quiz.explanation: 'À mon avis, c'est bon' — no 'que' after 'à mon avis.' The opinion follows directly.

quiz.q: Opinion-introducing phrases are compared to ___ in this week's analogy.
opts: doorways leading to entirely different rooms
different doorways leading into the same room
a single locked door with no entry
quiz.explanation: All three phrases lead to the same destination (your personal opinion), but 'je crois/pense que' have an extra step ('que') while 'à mon avis' lets you walk straight in.

quiz.q: These phrases signal to the listener that ___.
opts: a personal viewpoint is about to follow, not a stated fact
nothing meaningful is about to be said
the speaker is about to change the subject entirely
a definite, undisputed fact is about to follow
quiz.explanation: Opinion phrases clearly mark what follows as a personal viewpoint, distinguishing it from objective fact.

quiz.q: Which of these phrases requires 'que' before the opinion?
quiz.explanation: 'Je pense que...' requires 'que.' 'À mon avis' stands alone without 'que.'
